column1: # THE LIVE FIGHT -- append-only, and the current state is DERIVED.
# *** WHY THIS FILE EXISTS ***
# A fight runs ten messages. Across them the DM was holding, in his own
# narration and nowhere else: the round number, the initiative order, who was
# engaged with what, WHO HAD HELD AN ACTION, each monster's remaining hit
# points, who was surprised, what was spiked, and the light. Re-read every turn
# out of his own previous messages.
# That is the "narrate from my own summary instead of from the log" failure
# operating in THE HIGHEST-STAKES CONTEXT IN THE GAME -- and the worst single
# error of the campaign happened in exactly that context:
#   DAY 70, round 285. The DM RESOLVED THE PARTY'S ROUND WITHOUT ASKING. He
#   decided Yrtone swapped sling for flail, decided which four engaged, decided
#   nobody fired a missile, cast, dropped a load or withdrew. Four attack rolls
#   were VOIDED. The player: "Please stop right now."
# *** THE GATE ***
# `combat.py round` REFUSES to roll for a character who has no `declare` row in
# the current round. The CHECKLIST rule -- THE DM DOES NOT DECLARE THE PARTY'S
# ACTIONS, EVER, ASK -- stops being a sentence and becomes a required argument.
# It is a speed bump and not a wall (the DM could type a declaration the player
# never made), but it lands at the exact instant of the error, which is what
# made `party.py move` hold.
# verbs
#   start       a fight begins. detail = where, and what was met
#   surprise    a surprise roll and its reading
#   initiative  a round's initiative, party vs monsters
#   declare     *** WHAT THE PLAYER SAID A CHARACTER DOES. The gate reads this
#               and nothing else. One row per actor per round. ***
#   attack      a swing resolved (combat.py writes these)
#   damage      hit points off a MONSTER. Character damage stays in hp_log.tsv
#   hold        an action deliberately held
#   move        position changed inside the fight
#   morale      a morale check and its result
#   flee        a combatant leaves
#   dead        a combatant is down for good
#   end         the fight is over. detail = the outcome
# `side` is `party` or `monsters`. `actor` is a character name or a monster id
# ("trog1"), so two of a kind can be told apart -- which no prose narration of
# a four-monster fight has ever managed reliably.
# EMPTY BY DESIGN as of 2026-09-11: no fight is in progress. Expedition 9 is
# declared and has not begun.

column10: (24,37), the corner where the y=37 corridor turns north. Wandering check fired at round 35. Two came down the x=24 corridor from the north. BOTH SIDES SURPRISED: party d6=4 (troglodyte chameleon skin, surprised on 1-4 BY SIGHT), wanderers d6=2. DMG p.62: lesser subtracts from greater, so the party is inactive 2 SEGMENTS and the wanderers attack each segment AS IF IT WERE A FULL ROUND. Per-character DEX adjustment (DMG p.62): TRISTLE DEX 18 +3 negates all of it and is NOT SURPRISED; DELLIE DEX 4 -2 is surprised 4 segments, two longer than everyone else. Encounter distance: DMG p.62 light reliance caps at 2x lantern radius = 60 ft; d6=4 -> 40 ft, minus the surprise value of 4 -> 10 ft, ADJACENT. Front rank Yrtone/Dave/Torsat all three in (24,37) -- DMG p.97 gives a 10-ft corridor a frontage of three

NOT SURPRISED. DEX 18 = +3 Reaction/Attacking (PHB p.11), and DMG p.62 lets an individual negate that many segments of surprise for himself alone. Party base is 2 segments; 2-3 = 0. He is the only one of the eight who can act in the surprise window, and he has 2 SEGMENTS, each usable as a full round

SURPRISED 4 SEGMENTS, not 2. DEX 4 = -2 Reaction/Attacking, and DMG p.62 makes a dexterity PENALTY cost that many ADDITIONAL segments. She is still surprised for 2 segments after the rest of the party recovers

column6: Dave, Torsat, Yrtone, Frython, Ista, Blartho
column10: SURPRISED 2 SEGMENTS (party 4 minus wanderers 2, DMG p.62). No DEX reaction adjustment: Dave 10, Torsat 11, Yrtone 12, Frython 14, Ista 13, Blartho 12 all fall in the 0 band of rules/abilities.md

REVULSION ODOR, MM p.97, save vs poison (DMG p.79 Paralyzation/Poison/Death column). Front rank only, in contact at (24,37) -- the same scope applied on expeditions 3 and 4. Dave d20=4 vs 14 FAILED, 1d6=1 round. Torsat d20=17 vs 14 SAVED. Yrtone d20=4 vs 10 FAILED, 1d6=3 rounds. *** DAVE 18/26 -> 17 AT THE END OF ROUND 1, WHICH COSTS HIM +3 DAMAGE AND LEAVES +1 (PHB p.9 via rules/abilities.md) AND THE LOSS LASTS 10 MELEE ROUNDS AFTER THE FINAL EFFECT. *** Yrtone 14 -> 13 -> 12 -> 11 over rounds 1-3; no band change, no mechanical effect

SHOUTS a warning AND fires his short bow -- ONE ARROW AT EACH of the two. Player's words: 'He will shout while firing his bow - one shot at each of the troglodytes.' The shout is free and returns nobody a segment (rules/combat.md, 'What does NOT end a surprise once it is rolled'). Two arrows at his normal rate of 2 -- NO 3x, because that belongs to the surprising side and he is not it. Each at +0: +3 DEX 18, +1 elf short bow, -4 shooting past three allies who FILL a 10-ft corridor. 10 ft is short range for a short bow (to 50 ft), no range modifier. *** ON EACH MISS, 50% CHANCE IT STRIKES THE ALLY IN FRONT. ***

Segment 1: trog1 -> Torsat (d3=3), 11/4/2 all MISS vs AC 3. trog2 -> Dave (d3=2), 3 MISS, 19 HIT claw 1d3=1, 2 MISS. Segment 2: BOTH chose Torsat (d3=3, d3=3). trog1 claw 13 HIT 1, claw 16 HIT 3, bite 13 HIT 3 = SEVEN on a six-hit-point fighter. trog2 7/6/1 all MISS. *** TORSAT -1/6, unconscious, bleeding 1 hp per round to -10 unless somebody AIDS him (DMG p.82). *** Tristle's own arrow had already put Yrtone 7->2. Dave 9->8
attacks with her flail, from one knee at 2/7
attacks with his long sword -- BUT is inside Frython's sleep circle by the player's own geometry, so if the spell lands first he never swings

DROPS THE BOW AND TAKES UP A SPEAR. Costs the WHOLE ROUND, no attack (rules/combat.md, changing weapons in melee). Spear is -3 for him forever -- Thief non-proficiency, PHB p.37 -- which combat.py has applied to all five of his previous spear attacks. He is doing it because a spear reaches the front rank from the second and a long sword does not, and Hask, who held that job, is on the wool road
BANDAGES TORSAT -- aid under DMG p.82, which stops the bleeding the instant it is given, no roll. She sets the lantern down to do it; the light stays where it is

casts SLEEP. 1-segment casting time, the fastest thing on the table. 30-ft circle placed to cover both troglodytes -- 2 HD each, 2d4 affected, so BOTH, no saving throw. PLAYER'S GEOMETRY: they came in on Torsat's side, so DAVE (middle, beside Torsat) IS CAUGHT AUTOMATICALLY and YRTONE (far side, ~7 ft off) IS NOT
casts CURE LIGHT WOUNDS on YRTONE -- keeping a fighting cleric upright rather than buying back a man who is out for a week either way under the rule adopted today

SLING -> FLAIL and stands ready. The swap is FREE (rules/combat.md, the sling exemption) so it costs her nothing. She is in the THIRD rank and has no target regardless. Surprised through segments 1-2 of this round -- 2 left of her 4 -- so she cannot go first whatever initiative says, but 2 segments of 10 is not a lost round and she acts
SLAIN HELPLESS by Dave's long sword. PHB p.68: 'sleeping creatures can be slain automatically at a rate of 1 per slayer per melee round' -- no roll, no damage dice
SLAIN HELPLESS by Yrtone's flail, same rule, second slayer

BOTH TROGLODYTES SLAIN HELPLESS, round 2. Party won initiative 6-3; sleep casts in 1 segment, the fastest thing in the round, so it landed before any weapon moved. 2d4=2 against their 2 HD -- but THREE bodies were inside the circle, and PHB p.68 gives NO priority rule in 1e ('lowest hit dice first' is Basic/2e). Rolled neutrally for who it ran out before: d3=3, DAVE ESCAPED. Both of them went down asleep and were killed automatically, 1 per slayer per round -- Dave's long sword and Yrtone's flail. COST: Torsat -1/6, bandaged by Ista and stable, comatose then out a week. Yrtone took FIVE from Tristle's own arrow and was cured back to 6/7 by Blartho. Dave 8/9
